Class SlotGroups

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.slot.SlotGroups
public final class SlotGroups extends Object
Every slot group anyone has declared, with no menu open: the menu-free half of the slot group registry. SlotGroupCategories.groups(AbstractContainerMenu) is the per-menu half, the groups actually on a menu with their slots.

Where declarations come from

  • Vanilla: MenuKit declares one group per vanilla category at init (SlotGroupId.category(category)), the groups its resolvers produce. A mod that registers a resolver for its own menu declares its categories' groups the same way, with declare(SlotGroupId, SlotGroupCategory).
  • Created: MenuKit-Containers declares each group as it registers. A container-panel group (ContainerPanel.define(...).register()) registers at init, so it is listed from the title screen. A group built with a menu (CreatedSlots.onto(menu, player)) registers when that menu is built, so it is listed only after the first one; to list it from the title screen, its mod declares it at init too.
Declaring is idempotent. A group's category is fixed by its first declaration; a later one may add the group to a SlotGroupSet. A contradiction (a second category, a second set) is logged and ignored, never thrown: a listing is not worth crashing a player's game over.

For a settings screen

listing() is the player-facing list: each SlotGroups.Entry is a lone group or a set of groups, with a name and the categories in it (to filter by). It is cached, and rebuilt only after a declaration changes it.

Saving a choice

Save by group: SlotGroupId.asString() is the persisted key. A choice the player makes on a set's row is a choice for each group in SlotGroups.Entry.groups(); store it under each of their ids. A group's id never changes, whatever sets exist, so a saved choice survives a mod adding, renaming or dropping a set. SlotGroups.Entry.key() is for the listing: it matches a row to what is shown. It is not for saving.

Who may put a group in a set

Only the group's own declaration, in the group's own namespace (a category group's category namespace; a created group's panel-id namespace), and only its first. Anything else is an error (§0063): no mod can move another mod's group between rows, and no row changes under a screen that has already shown it.

Names

Translatable, on keys derived from the id, the way slot operations are named; the declaring mod ships the lines and a missing line shows the key: 
slot_group.menukit.player_hotbar                    a vanilla group: slot_group.<category namespace>.<category path>
slot_group.inventorymax.equipment_elytra.elytra     a created group: slot_group.<panel id>.<group id>, lowercased, other characters as dots
slot_group_set.inventorymax.pockets                 a set: slot_group_set.<namespace>.<path>
A group inside a set is listed under the set's name, so its own line is optional.

Source

source(SlotGroupId) names the mod a row comes from, so a screen can say "Pockets (Inventory Max)". It is null for vanilla's groups. For anything else it is the mod whose namespace the row is named in: a set's namespace, a created group's panel-id namespace (the part before the colon), or a mod's own category's namespace. The name is that mod's display name from its fabric.mod.json, or the namespace itself when no loaded mod has that id. A created group whose panel id has no namespace has no known source, and is null too.

The group a slot is in

of(SlotRef) answers for one slot, the way a SlotOperations veto sees it: the created group a mod declared for a created slot, the vanilla group of a vanilla slot's category on its menu, and for a player-inventory slot with no menu (world pickup) the vanilla group its index sits in. A veto uses it to tell a hotbar slot from a pocket.
